result:
I tested 6 properties on `setuptools.package_index` (setuptools 78.1.0): 2 found real bugs, and the other 4 passed.

**Bug 1 — writing files outside `tmpdir` (High, Logic).** `PackageIndex.download(url, tmpdir)` says a URL "is downloaded to a subpath of `tmpdir`". It isn't when the URL contains `%2F`. The filename is taken from the last part of the URL with percent-escapes decoded, so `%2F` turns into `/` and the name becomes an absolute path. `os.path.join(tmpdir, name)` then throws `tmpdir` away.
- Hypothesis shrank it to `https://example.com/%2F`, which resolves to `/`.
- I confirmed it end to end against a local HTTP server: `download()` wrote the server's response to a path outside `tmpdir`.
- This is CVE-2025-47273, which is what this checkout is for. The suggested fix rejects any resolved filename that doesn't start with `tmpdir`.

**Bug 2 — slow scanning of downloaded pages (Medium).** `find_external_links` runs the `REL` regex over every index page it downloads. On a page with many `<` and no `>`, the time grows with the square of the page size:

| Page size (chars) | Time |
|---|---|
| 16k | 0.96 s |
| 32k | 3.76 s |
| 64k | 15.2 s |

The cause is the unbounded `[^>]*` at the start of the regex; the earlier ReDoS fix (CVE-2022-40897) only bounded the `\s{0,10}` parts. Changing `[^>]` to `[^<>]` makes it linear: 256k characters now take 5 ms, and a normal `rel="download"` tag still matches.

**Passed:**
- `_encode_auth` decodes back to its input and never adds a newline.
- `_vcs_split_rev_from_url` returns the right clean URL and revision.
- `htmldecode` agrees with `html.unescape` on well-formed entities.
- `interpret_distro_name` splits the name from the version correctly.

I didn't hand-build a failing input for these four to prove each test could catch a fault, so a pass is weaker evidence than it looks.

One change during testing: the URL path `.` resolves to `tmpdir` itself. That's a failed download, not an escape, so I relaxed "strictly inside `tmpdir`" to "not outside `tmpdir`" and recorded the change in `claims.md`.

All files are in `runs/setuptools-pkgindex_v2_r2/`:
- `claims.md`
- `test_package_index.py`
- `repro_traversal.py`
- `bug_report_setuptools_package_index_PackageIndex_download_2026-10-28_18-06_mm1f.md`
- `bug_report_setuptools_package_index_find_external_links_2026-10-28_18-06_xsb5.md`
